findings.F1: The book's deepest fall, -44.7 % over 313 days, spans windows w12 to w14, while the coins fell -68.2 % in the same days. Window w14 alone lost a summed -36.5 % of daily returns. The book's mean daily return was -0.115 % in w12–w14 against +0.064 % in the other windows, which sinks both the Calmar (0.29) and the mean daily return (0.042 %).
findings.F2: The 15 entries taken in w12–w14 returned -14.1 % on average while held, with 20 % winners. The other 113 entries returned +15.7 % with 63 % winners. The two groups differ in the coin's 90-day (540-bar) return before entry, -23.5 % against +37.1 %, but not in its 14-day (84-bar) return, +13.2 % against +9.9 %.
findings.F3: The rebound grows with the coin's longer trend before the panic. By tercile of the 30-day (180-bar) return, held returns were +5.3 %, +8.3 % and +14.5 % (31 cases each). By tercile of the distance from the 30-day mean price they were +3.9 %, +9.8 % and +14.2 %. By tercile of the 90-day return they were +4.3 %, +1.1 % and +15.4 %, with 100 % winners in the top tercile (8 cases; slope of the 84-bar return on it, t 0.95, 23 cases). The 9 entries of 2018 lost -33.4 % on average.
findings.F4: What happens in the first day after entry sorts the outcome. Entries whose coin rose more than 4.3 % over the next 24 hours returned +34.3 % on average while held (median +11.9 %, 43 cases). The other two terciles returned +2.6 % and -0.6 %. Over the first 72 hours, the top tercile returned +34.7 % against -2.4 % and +4.1 %.
findings.F5: The size of the panic does not add to the rebound. By tercile of the range ratio, the mildest stretches (3.0–3.16 times the usual range) returned +15.2 % while held, against +6.2 % and +6.6 % for the stronger ones. The deepest tercile of the 24-hour fall returned +4.4 %, against +17.2 % and +15.1 %, in line with the flat slope of the verdict (t 0.49).
findings.F6: The cost of trading is not the cause. The total move per case, +5.71 %, is 29.6 times the 0.19 % trade cost. The book's mean daily return is low because the book holds a position on only 16 % of coin-days (0.26 % a day in position), with 0.021 trades a day.

ideas.idea: Among 24-hour stretches where a coin's range is several times its 30-day average, the deeper the coin's fall over that stretch, the higher its return over the next 14 days, only while the coin's 90-day return is positive, and the more so the larger that 90-day rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys panics in coins whose last three months rose, and refuses panics inside a longer decline, where the forced selling is part of a bear market rather than a one-off discount.
ideas.name: panic rebound in uptrends

ideas.idea: Among 24-hour stretches where a coin's range is several times its 30-day average and the coin fell, the larger the coin's rise over the 24 hours after the stretch, the higher its return over the following 14 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader waits one day after a panic and buys in proportion to the first bounce, which shows that the forced selling is over.
ideas.name: confirmed panic bounce continues

ideas.idea: Among 24-hour stretches where a coin's range is well above its 30-day average, the deeper the coin's fall over that stretch, the higher its return over the next 14 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader can apply the liquidity premium to moderate shake-outs as well as extreme panics, holding a position more often for the same edge per trade.
ideas.name: moderate shake-outs also rebound
